A dialog on a veil is the one place the grammar dims the page. Without it the backdrop competes with the sheet.
Ink is the accent when the theme is monochrome, so it is the most-used colour in the system.
One family, so hierarchy is weight, size and ink strength. Three strengths of ink is the whole secondary/tertiary vocabulary; the portfolio is set in exactly these three.
The label colour. Every kicker, key and rule-line is faint ink, never the accent — a coloured label is a second voice.
Text on a filled action. When the accent is ink, the label on it is the page colour; that pair is the monochrome button.

Monochrome by default is not the absence of an accent — it is an accent compiled to ink. The gate stays open because colour is a choice the seeds can still make, and one filled action per surface needs one colour to be filled with.
The one hover step a filled action gets. Cutting it left a primary button that answered a hover with nothing at all, which reads as a dead control.
The label on the accent. Derived by the engine so a chromatic accent still carries a readable label.
The wash is the hover on ghost actions and the selection tint — Visionary’s --sel. It is the accent’s only appearance on a surface.
A tinted rule for the one selected thing. Everything else is drawn in --line.
The grammar draws with lines: every card, row, panel and ledger is a 1px rule. This is the most-used non-ink token and the thing shadows were cut in favour of.
The rule for an edge that has to hold on its own — a panel border, a table head. One step, not a scale.
Keyboard focus stays visible in every theme. Not a taste question.
Status is ink and a word; the colour confirms, never carries. Kept because a status that is only text is slower to scan in a console.
As positive.
As positive. Danger is never only a colour.
The wash behind a status badge. The badge is a filled pill, so it needs one fill that is not the ink.
As positive-soft.
As positive-soft.

Lines, not shadows. The reference grammar — the portfolio and Visionary alike — draws every level with a 1px rule and an alpha wash, and paints no drop shadow anywhere; a shadow is decoration the eye pays for on every card. The elevation tokens keep their offsets and paint nothing, so the rule does the work it was already doing.
The tap acknowledgement.
Hover and focus. Visionary’s chrome answers in 120–160ms.
A sheet or a toast entering.
The ground changing. A theme flip is the one slow transition the site has, and it should be seen.
One curve, an ease-out, the way the portfolio’s --ease is one curve.

Nothing bounces. The engine gives a calm theme a spring on emphasis above energy 0.3, and a dialog that overshoots is a personality the chrome should not have. Collapses to the ordinary curve; the energy dial still sets speed.
Density is a dial the owner of a screen turns, not a taste. Kept at 1.
A control rounds a little — 6–8px at calm energy — so a row of them reads as instruments rather than boxes.
A panel rounds a little more than a control. The portfolio’s panels are 10px; this compiles to 12px at the house energy.

Two radii, not three: a control and a panel. The engine gave overlays 2.4× the control radius, which at calm energy is a 19px dialog — the one soft shape on an otherwise architectural page. An overlay is a panel; it rounds like one.
